BeatScope measures a song; Beathi turns the measurements into a film. Everything runs on your machine.

## What's new

### High-precision beat tracking

A new mode hands the beat work to the Beat This model and keeps everything BeatScope does around it - onsets, energy, tempo, the film, the exports. Turn it on per song with the **Standard / High precision** button in the studio, or from the command line:

```powershell
beatscope analyze song.wav --backend enhanced --model-device cuda
```

### The meter stays what it is

A song in 3/4 is no longer reported as 4/4, and beats past the end of the analysed grid are counted in the song's own meter. Projects also say when a meter or a tempo was assumed rather than measured, instead of presenting an assumption as a finding.

### Benchmarks you can check

Runs state how many tracks they scored and how many failed, and a run under one configuration can no longer reuse predictions made under another.

## How it measures

| Corpus | What it is | Beat F1 | Downbeat F1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GTZAN, 999 tracks | held out - the model never trained on it | **0.8909** | **0.7871** |
| Ballroom, 349 tracks | in the model's training data | 0.9908 | 0.9875 |

The first row is the number to read. The second is what a corpus the model has already seen looks like, and it is there so the difference is visible rather than implied.

## Install

```powershell
pip install "beatscope[public-benchmark]"
```

The model weights download on first use; point `TORCH_HOME` at a cache to reuse ones you already have. Details, including what the mode does not do, are in [high-precision mode](docs/high-precision.md).

## Known limits

- Classical and piano material is weaker (0.66-0.63 across two corpora).
- Songs that change tempo mid-way: the beats are mostly right, the sequence is not always tracked through the change.
- The checkpoint's licence has not been reviewed for redistribution.

Two ideas were measured and left out of this release - a second onset extractor and a local timing refinement. Both are in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) with their numbers.
